title: AI Agents Are Already Changing the Price of Goods
title_cn: AI Agents Are Already Changing the Price of Goods
summary: It's obvious that things are getting more expensive, and there are plenty of reasons behind the surge in prices — whether it's wars or inflation or companies padding their profit margins. But with the release of AI agents like Meta's Muse, tech companies are promising consumers that agents will start saving them tons of money by finding the best deals. According to today's guest, Lindsay Owens, the history of price gouging does not bode well for claims that things might get cheaper because of new technology, and research conducted by her think tank Groundwork Collaborative shows that a number of consumer facing agents end up serving customers more expensive items after learning more about their financial situation. Her new book Gouged: The End of a Fair Price — and What That Means for Your Wallet gets into the history of how companies got away with charging more for their goods, through means like data collection and surveillance. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Johannesburg’s Infrastructure Crisis Puts South Africa’s Investment at Risk
title_cn: Johannesburg’s Infrastructure Crisis Puts South Africa’s Investment at Risk
summary:
Power cuts, water shortages and crumbling roads are undermining Johannesburg’s economy and threatening its ability to retain businesses and attract investment. Can South Africa’s City of Gold turn itself around? On this episode of Next Africa, Jennifer Zabasajja examines the financial pressures and political instability behind Johannesburg’s decline, and whether upcoming local elections could help change its course.
Business Leadership South Africa CEO Busi Mavuso explains why companies are being forced to work around failing public services. Ninety One founder and CEO Hendrik du Toit discusses the investment needed to rebuild the city, while Eskom CEO Dan Marokane explains how the utility moved from rolling blackouts to excess generating capacity—and why Johannesburg still faces outages. Plus, Bloomberg South Africa Bureau Chief Alex Parker assesses the city’s infrastructure backlog and prospects for recovery. 
 (Source: Bloomberg)

Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Brussels, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

Traders are bracing for steep losses across Brazilian markets after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva came from behind to win Brazil’s runoff election, halting a right-wing wave sweeping Latin America. 

President Trump said it’s “getting to be decision time” on whether he will make a deal with Tehran or resume attacks. European natural gas futures climbed to the highest since 2022.
